subject: ventures/trade-show-roi-calculator
professional: a trade-show or field-marketing manager who owns an exhibit budget and reports cost per lead and ROI to a sales VP

evidence.correctness: Ran node --test '*.test.mjs': 29 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed all 10 fixture shows (cost, cost per lead, cost per qualified lead, deals, gross profit, ROI, break-even leads) in an independent Python script: identical to the cent; best set under $40k found by exhaustive search over 1,024 subsets matches (Regional + FabTech, net $28,160). Own node fuzz (300 random years, budget and quarter cap, different generator) 0 mismatches. Guide worked example re-derived by hand. Fails: out-of-range options silently defaulted. The formulas are the standard (gain - cost) / cost ROI, cost / leads, cost / (leads x rate); I cite no CEIR benchmark because I could not verify one.
evidence.completeness: README CLI usage, stdin, budget, quarter cap, JSON, every-show and cheapest-first comparison, weak-lead re-check, break-even lead count: all ran. Gaps: closeBy date appears only in JSON; no stubs or TODOs found; sitemap and both pages exist and link each other (page.test.mjs).
evidence.verification: 29 tests pass, including a 300-year brute-force comparison and hand-arithmetic checks. 8 hand-seeded mutations: 5 core-math or solver mutations all caught (3 to 8 tests failing), 3 survived, all in advisory output (sales-cycle window, budget-unused threshold, closeBy). Core numbers are well guarded; findings text and dates are not.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (312 lines), cli.mjs, index.html script, tests. Pure functions, no deps, exact solver with cap, clear errors with line numbers. Deductions: readOptions silently falls back to defaults on bad values (a silent fallback), a dead sales-cycle condition, a computed-but-unshown field, 'late' recomputes a max inside a filter. Page and CLI share the engine, no copied logic.
evidence.claims: Served page and llms.txt on https://marisstella.app/trade-show-roi-calculator/ load (200) and carry marisstella.app URLs; sitemap served with absolute URLs. Disclaimer, no-warranty, not-a-forecast on both pages and README; privacy claim true for engine and CLI; brute-force claim backed by a test. One unsourced and self-contradicted line ('fee often under half').
evidence.fitness: Walked an exhibitor's job: paste 10 shows, set funnel, get rank, buy/skip reasons, break-even and a budgeted plan: works end to end in one command, with a plain-language reason for each skipped show. The user must fold drayage, labour and lead-retrieval costs into swag and must notice silent default substitution.
evidence.domain: A trade-show marketing manager or event ROI analyst would accept the cost-per-lead / cost-per-qualified-lead / ROI / break-even leads framing, and appreciate the weak-lead re-check and budget optimisation. They would ask for itemised exhibit costs (space, build, shipping, I&D labour, lead retrieval), pipeline versus closed revenue, and the sales-cycle timing that the tool tries to flag. Awareness and existing-customer meetings are disclosed as out of scope. No external benchmark (CEIR, Exhibitor Magazine) cited or verified.

checks.what: Sales-cycle finding ('deals close after the year ends')
checks.method: behaviour vs its message, cycles 6, 12, 24 months on a Jan and a Dec show
checks.expected: fires when a spring-show deal lands after year end (guide: 6-month cycle, spring show -> autumn)
checks.observed: fires only at 24 months; rule compares to latest chosen show + 365 days, so it is never true for cycles up to 12 months

mutations.change: staffCount * staffDays * staffDayCost -> staffCount * staffDayCost (drop staff days)
closeBy = day + cycle -> closeBy = day (ignore sales cycle)

defects.what: Rates outside range are silently replaced by defaults in readOptions (close 150 -> 20, margin 120 -> 60, ltv 0 -> 1, bad budget -> 0); the CLI only checks >= 0 and the page's max= attributes are hints, so a typo changes the answer with no message and exit 0

Sales-cycle finding is logically dead for cycles up to 12 months: lateness is measured against the latest chosen show date + 365, so c.day + cycle > max.day + 365 cannot hold; the guide advertises exactly the 6-month case. Mutating the window constant leaves all 29 tests green
No test covers the findings (sales-cycle, budget-unused) or closeBy: 3 of 8 seeded mutations survived, all in these advisory outputs

Cost model has four fields; drayage/shipping, booth build and installation and dismantle labour, lead retrieval, pre-show marketing and utilities have no home except being folded into 'swag and collateral', and the input notes do not say so
Guide says the booth fee is 'often under half' of total cost with no source; its own example (59.7%) and the fixture (47-58%) contradict it
closeBy (sales-cycle close date) is computed but shown nowhere except --json; CLI help and cycle input imply it is visible
Quoted thousands-separated amounts ("1,200") split on the comma and produce two misleading field errors; README only warns about commas in names

verdict: The arithmetic is right and the optimiser is exact: every number I recomputed independently (10 shows, budget optimum, 300 fuzzed years) matched, and the served page, llms.txt and disclaimers check out, so it meets the bar. It is held back by silent substitution of defaults for out-of-range rates (a typo changes the answer with exit 0), a sales-cycle warning that cannot fire for a normal 6-month cycle although the guide advertises it, three advisory outputs no test pins (3 of 8 seeded mutations survived), and a four-field cost model that omits the exhibit costs a field marketer budgets for. No high-severity defect.
